findings.reason: state the intended relationship with supported metadata, or explicitly remove the apparent ordering requirement, so scheduling follows the authored intent without accidentally gating this plan on the entire active predecessor.
findings.text: The predecessor is declared only through plan-after, which is absent from the documented relationship vocabulary and produces relations: {} in read_plan; consequently the apparent relationship to work-flows-to-the-lane is invisible to machine readers.

findings.reason: declare a durable expected population and a control containing a known missing run, with that run required to appear as missing, so the zero result can demonstrate preservation.
findings.text: The required live-home census must find runs removed during the last day with no pointer or record, but it names no independently retained population of requests/runs against which those absent entries can be compared; a scan of survivors can report zero even when the reported disappearance recurs.

findings.reason: give independently shippable outcomes separate section verdicts and controls, so one successful fix cannot close unrelated unfinished work.
findings.text: Section 10 couples stopping automatic repair loops with retaining every folded finding in repair advice, while section 14 at line 268 couples decision scoping, ordered edit visibility, flag coercion, followup defaults and sprint discovery; these outcomes can succeed or fail independently.

findings.reason: distinguish literal data from unresolved required inputs and retain a refusal control for a genuinely incomplete command inside a code span, rather than making formatting determine whether intent is complete.
findings.text: Defects D36 and D120 describe literal path patterns and HTML test data being mistaken for placeholders or instructions, but the deliverable exempts all code-span text; an actually unfinished command such as a project argument containing an unresolved placeholder would now pass solely because it is formatted as code.

findings.reason: distinguish duplicate coverage from distinct nodes contributing to one section, and require both a true duplicate refusal and acceptance of a legitimate second piece before treating the section as already delivered.
findings.text: Any live, delivered, promoted or landed implementation run is specified to hold its entire section, although the cited defect register explicitly withdraws D9 because three nodes on one section were an intentional context-fit split; the new rule would block the remaining pieces after the first piece exists or lands.

findings.reason: require evidence that ownership ended or was revoked and a control in which a live holder on another host retains its lock, so a fleet move cannot admit overlapping promotion or resume work.
findings.text: Section 9 treats a holder on any host other than the current fleet node as no longer working, and line 192 requires releasing a foreign-host reservation without proving that holder has stopped; the cited old-node incidents establish stale holders, not that every remote holder is stale.
